archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area distributor)
archetype.definition: A veteran stopgap who wins by getting the ball out quickly and accurately underneath and over the middle, and who gives back value whenever he pushes the ball downfield or the down-and-distance gets long.

report.headline: Accurate underneath, broken deep, and propped up by trailing-script volume
report.take:
Brissett is what he has been for a decade: a big, calm pocket passer who throws on time and rarely makes a wild throw, but who does not stretch a defense. His bad-throw rate of 9% ranks 9th of 36, and his tracking CPOE of +5.5 says the ball is going where it should. The other side shows up in his 5.58 yards per attempt, 42nd of 43 qualifiers. His career aDOT has sat between 7.1 and 9.1 every season, so the short game is no scheme accident. It is who he is.

The season splits sharply by depth. On 152 throws between the line of scrimmage and 19 air yards he has been good: +0.20 EPA on short throws with a 77.6% completion rate, and +0.44 on intermediate throws. At the two ends of the field it falls apart. His 26 throws behind the line lose 0.38 a play, and his 19 deep attempts have produced three completions and three interceptions at -0.545 EPA. That deep sample is small, but it accounts for three of his five picks and most of the damage. He has also been noticeably more aggressive than usual, throwing into tight windows 24.6% of the time against 16-18% in past seasons, and the 3-INT game against the Giants, when that rate hit 45.7%, shows the cost.

The totals flatter him in one way and hide something in another. A defense ranked 31st against the pass and last in explosive passes allowed keeps putting Arizona behind, and 85 of his 214 dropbacks have come trailing by 9+. In those snaps he is at +0.205 EPA with a 75.6% completion rate, much of it against soft coverage. In one-score games he drops to -0.164, and on 18 fourth-quarter plays in close games he is at -0.90. Third downs (33.9% converted, 7.2 yards to go on average) are where drives stall. What the numbers undersell is his pocket play: a 19.4% pressure-to-sack rate, 10th of 36 and much better than last year's 28.5%, helped by a quicker 2.62-second release.

The line is now a real problem. Left tackle Paris Johnson Jr., a 100%-snap starter, is on IR with a February return date, and guard Isaiah Adams joined him before Week 5. That was the five-sack game against Detroit. Expect more of what Brissett already is: quick throws, a lot of volume because the defense cannot get stops, solid fantasy totals, and below-average efficiency whenever the game is close.

strengths.title: Short and intermediate timing game
strengths.body: Between the line and 19 air yards he completes passes at well above expectation and creates positive EPA. That comes from a quick, on-time release and accurate ball placement, not from YAC luck. Precision underneath has been the steadiest part of his career, so this should hold.

strengths.title: Pressure handled without the sack
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate has dropped from 28.5% last year to 19.4%, and his time to throw is down about three-tenths of a second from 2025. Getting the ball out faster is the cause, which makes this a skill change rather than luck. That matters even more with two starting linemen on IR.

strengths.title: McBride as the reliable outlet
strengths.body: Trey McBride leads the team with 56 targets at +0.29 EPA a target, the most productive high-volume connection on the roster. Kendrick Bourne has been efficient on a smaller share. Brissett's offense works when it runs through the tight end over the middle, where his overall EPA is +0.34.

concerns.title: The deep ball is a turnover machine
concerns.body: Three completions and three interceptions on 19 deep attempts. His career aDOT suggests the deep game was never a strength, and the jump in tight-window throws is pushing him into it more often. Some of the 15.8% completion rate will normalize on a bigger sample, but this will stay the weak spot.

concerns.title: Efficiency vanishes when it's close
concerns.body: His positive numbers come mostly while trailing by 9+. In one-score games and the fourth quarter of close games he has been a clear negative, and third downs are a drag. This is the gap between a starter and a stopgap, and his career EPA ranks say it is longstanding, not a slump.

concerns.title: A gutted left side of the line
concerns.body: Johnson is out for the season and Adams until at least early November. The first game without them produced five sacks. His quick release softens the blow, but fewer clean pockets will cap the intermediate throws that drive his value.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung back and forth, from +9 to -8.1 to +10.1 to -18.2 to +3. The good games were high-volume shootouts, and the bad ones came when Seattle squeezed him underneath and the Giants baited him into three picks. Week 5's 292 yards came with a career-high-for-the-year 9.9 intended air yards but also five sacks behind a patched line.

nextGame.headline: Volume should come, but the Rams take away what's left
nextGame.body:
Los Angeles is built to make Brissett live underneath. It ranks 1st in deep EPA allowed and 4th in explosive pass rate allowed, holds tight ends to -0.23 EPA a target (2nd), and has allowed the second-fewest passing yards a game to quarterbacks. Opponents have thrown to running backs 23.7% of the time against a league norm of 18.2%, which points to a lot of checkdowns, and Jeremiyah Love has been inefficient as a receiver. The opening is that the Rams allow 2 passing TDs a game (21st), and a 13.5-point spread with a Rams offense that passes well above expectation means Arizona should be throwing 40-plus times.

Availability helps him up front. Myles Garrett is on IR and not expected back at practice this week, and the Rams' pass rush already ranks 27th in hit rate and 24th in sack rate. That is the softest rush he can hope for with Johnson and Adams out. His own report is clean (full participation), and the game is indoors.

keyMatchups.title: Rams' deep shell vs his deep woes
keyMatchups.body: The league's stingiest deep defense meets a quarterback averaging -0.545 EPA on deep throws. If he forces shots, this is where interceptions come from. If he stays disciplined, his yards per attempt will sit around 5-6 again.

keyMatchups.title: McBride against a stingy TE defense
keyMatchups.body: His most productive target faces a defense ranked 2nd against tight ends by EPA and 4th by points over average. If McBride is muted, volume shifts to Michael Wilson, who has been at -0.14 EPA a target on 51 looks.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs a weak, Garrett-less rush
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's depleted left side gets a break against a Rams front that rarely hits the quarterback. That should keep the sack count closer to his season norm than to Week 5's five.

nextGame.watch: Whether he takes the checkdowns the Rams give him or keeps forcing tight-window and deep throws, which is where his interceptions have come from.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable for an ugly reason. Arizona's defense ranks 31st against the pass and last in explosives allowed, so he will keep throwing about 40 times a game from behind, and that keeps his fantasy floor in the mid-teens. The short-area accuracy and the improved pressure-to-sack rate fit how he has always played and should hold. The deep line should get less extreme with more attempts, but not into an asset. The red-zone TD output (9 TDs on 38 attempts despite a 52.6% completion rate) is likely to cool.

The bigger drag is the line. Johnson is gone for the year, and until Adams returns in November, expect more hits and fewer intermediate windows. Expect roughly 210-250 yards a game at a mediocre yards-per-attempt, with close to an interception a game, against a team record that is unlikely to improve.
swingFactors: How the line holds up without Johnson and Adams
Whether the Arizona defense keeps forcing trailing scripts
Whether he cuts down the tight-window and deep throws

bets.reason: Arizona is a 13.5-point underdog against a Rams offense that passes well above expectation, and Arizona's pass defense ranks 31st. He has already logged 85 dropbacks while trailing by 9+, so another catch-up script means volume.

The Rams take away deep throws and funnel targets to running backs at well above the league rate. That pushes him toward the short throws he completes at 77.6%, and his completion rate when trailing by 9+ is 75.6%.

He has thrown 5 picks in 5 games, with at least one in three of them. An increase in tight-window throws and a likely pass-heavy comeback script against the league's best deep defense point to at least one.

Arizona's last three games totaled 66, 60 and 66 points behind a defense ranked last in explosive passes allowed. The Rams' 10th-ranked offense should score, and the Rams' defense allows 2 passing TDs a game even while limiting yardage.

confidence.note: Five games and a 19-attempt deep sample, plus a fresh offensive-line change, though his profile matches a decade of career data.
